item.title: Bio-mechanical
item.description:
Parent: [[topics/medical]]. Human device and exposure rows already filed: [[topics/health/biomedical-catalogue]]. Patterning paper: [[posts/holey-graphene-molecular-stencil]].

Already on this archive

  • INBRAIN cortical interface, NCT06368310 — first-in-human intraoperative use; small set; Preliminary device data. [[topics/health/effects]]
  • Graphene / GO / GFET electrode and biosensor literature — high paper count, few cleared instruments.
  • Oriented GO/PCL fibres and conductive scaffolds — rat sciatic-gap and in-vitro axon-length reports. Animal. Preliminary translation.
  • Holey graphene as a molecular stencil on gold (2015) — fabrication toward sensors, not an implant.
  • Directa G+ textile membranes and printed thermal circuits — garments, not implants. [[topics/industry/directa-gplus]]
  • ZenGUARD on mask and HVAC media — coat on a filter, not a neural thread. [[topics/industry/zenguard]]

Goals people write down

  • A cortical or peripheral electrode that records or stimulates without a stainless-steel penalty in flexibility or site area.
  • A scaffold that is conductive enough for cells and resorbable enough for a surgeon.
  • A wearable (tattoo, textile, microneedle) that lasts a shift, not a press cycle.
  • Closed-loop interfaces. Still a review-article sentence in 2025–26.

Theories in circulation

  • “Graphene replaces silicon in diagnostics this decade.” Same foundry problem as the electronics pitch. [[logs/theories]]
  • A patterning paper “will treat” a named disease this cycle. Motivation language. [[logs/unsourced]]
  • Long-term implant / IV GO is solved. 2025–26 reviews still list cytotoxicity, dose, metals, and fate as open.

Projections (forecast language)

Patient-specific printed grafts, smart microneedles, injectable graphene, AI-designed scaffolds — review-article futures. They sit next to the NCT table, not in place of it.

item.title: Biology
item.description:
Parent: [[topics/medical]]. Exposure numbers and human protocols: [[topics/health]]. Form still decides the result: [[reference/forms]].

Already on this archive

  • Form × route matrix. [[topics/health/form-route]]
  • Occupational and small-human effects. [[topics/health/effects]]
  • Andrews 2024 / NCT03659864 GO inhalation — acute physiology, not ecology.
  • Rodent high-dose lung inflammation / fibrosis trend in some designs — size, oxidation, metals, respirable fraction. Same effects page.
  • In-vitro antibacterial / antiviral GO pile — large, condition-dependent. [[topics/health/biomedical-catalogue]]
  • GO as a carrier in cells and rodents (small-molecule, photothermal ideas) — delivery papers, not licensed drugs.

Goals people write down

  • A sheet that a cell treats as inert at a useful dose.
  • A sheet that a microbe does not ignore (antibacterial coatings, filter media — [[topics/industry/zenguard]] is a coat, not a drug).
  • Fate and clearance maps for GO vs rGO vs GNP after lung, gut, or skin contact.
  • Plant and soil studies that survive a second lab.

Theories in circulation

  • “Pencil lead, therefore biology is done.” Ignores GO vs monolayer vs powder. [[reference/misconceptions]]
  • “One IC50 in a dish predicts a workplace or a vaccine.” Wrong evidence class. [[topics/fringe]]
  • Oxidative-stress / sharp-edge cutting as the mechanism. Real papers exist; they do not collapse to one slogan.
  • Bioaccumulation as a cover-up story. Documented on [[logs/conspiracies]], not here as fact.

Projections (forecast language)

Reviews keep projecting biodegradable graphene, DNA–graphene scaffolds, and “green” GO from biomass. Treat as slides until there is an NCT number or a regulator text. Market-size “graphene healthcare” figures stay [[logs/unsourced]] unless the house and the definition are quoted.
